item.content:encoded:
Personally I love it the way it is with all it's flaws and cringey things. Every so often I come back to read it and it always makes me smile and remember the time I read it the first time - long ago back when Kondraki was writing and Site19 IRC were the classiest joint around and it brings back all the good memories of that time.

+ show block
– hide block

I'm not sure about the change. In my opinion this Tale is old enough that everyone who wanted to read it and vote on it already did and the only people reading it now are old folks reliving the memories or possibly some new folks reading about SCP history - and neither of these groups cares about the "writing quality" or possible cringines of the piece. It was a different time and in a way like the old skips this Tale is a picture of the past that we are able to look at thanks to internet saving things up unchanged for decades. And do remember that it is more than a decade old now. So if we could vote on comments (heh) I'd vote for keeping it as it is.

On the other hand I'm just an random old lurker and you're a living SCP legend and more importantly the author of this tale. Just please - if you change it let it keep it's spirit.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
The trouble is that the description for SCP-120 says:

The item will only function in this way if a number of variables are addressed: the subject must be genetically human; the subject must be conscious; the subject must be carrying weights of under the specified amount; and only one subject must be present on the surface.

So it's not possible for multiple people to carry SCP-531-D at once, and his description would lead me to believe that he weighs more than 37.8 kilograms.

Apologies if I seem like a dog with a bone here, my intention is not to annoy.
